title: Arranging for other bands and radio before 52nd Street
summary: Carter wrote for Miller, Dorsey and radio shows, then played Kelly Stables and the Famous Door.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: And you began at that time to do some arrangements, I think, for other bands.
Yes.
Who were some of those leaders that called on you to ...
Gee, I guess I did some things for -- well, I know I did some things for Glenn Miller and gee, did somebody say I did some things for Dorsey?
Yes.
I don't remember what I did. For Tommy Dorsey. Actually, that's a long time ago, but it's not so long that I shouldn't remember [someone.] I don't know --
I just did anything that I was called upon to do...
Well, yeah .. and you were doing these big band, or what came to be known as 'Swing arrangements', I presume?
Yes. Some of those. I did some writing for some radio shows. Oh, I did ...
You mean the Lucky Strike ...
Yeah.
But that came a bit later, though, didn't it?
Yeah, that did come a bit later.
That came in '42?
Yes, and ...
But before that, you made your bow at 52nd Street?
Yes.
I think you took a group in to the Kelly Stables.
And then the Famous Door.
Yeah, this was late '41 and early '42.
Right. Right.
